recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-15722 unless a future work group decision changes language binding policy or HealthcareService search parameter design.
issue_request: FHIR-15722 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request asking to add HealthcareService.communication (0..*) as a CodeableConcept bound to the language value set so HealthcareService can declare languages spoken or offered at the service level rather than deriving them from PractitionerRole.
initial_application: Historical commit bd89a75a69 explicitly names GF#15722 and added HealthcareService.communication to the then-authoritative HealthcareService spreadsheet. Later source refactoring transformed the resource into the current XML StructureDefinition and search parameter bundle while retaining the element.
additional_context: FHIR-17379 duplicated the request with languageOffered/search wording. Current source/fhir.ini lists HealthcareService as an active resource. The current binding uses the modern common-language pattern, required all-languages with languages as a starter/additional value set, preserving the approved language concept while matching current terminology conventions. FHIR-25302 later added Location extensions that mimic HealthcareService.communication, confirming the element is established design.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed: the active HealthcareService StructureDefinition already has HealthcareService.communication as 0..* CodeableConcept with language binding metadata and explanatory service-level text, and the HealthcareService-communication token search parameter targets that element.

related_jiras.note: Duplicate request for a HealthcareService languageOffered element and search support; it supports the same current-source conclusion but is not an independent issue to decide.
Later PA decision for Location language extensions explicitly mimicked HealthcareService.communication, supporting that the HealthcareService element is intentional current design.
